git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches SKILL.md (the testing row of the reference table, a new Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, the Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call rule, the do: rule and step 1 of Before you finish) and renames references/testing.md to references/ex_unit.md with a changed Assert with patterns rule. macros.md and library-design.md are unchanged, so the seven macro and library rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: validation in a @doc false function called from a one-line quote is clean under Keep quote blocks small; the use documentation rule needs an admonition at the top of @moduledoc; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden for every __ function and macro in all five runs); `if not ... raise` validation is not counted under the branching rule; a one-line multi-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; String.to_atom on route text from source code (haiku-1 line 101, haiku-2 line 110, sonnet-2 line 121) is not counted under the atom rule.

Changed rule, graded against its current text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability): Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. Since 3e3581d the sentences "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line. When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks." were replaced by "A function may mix the forms: a short clause on `do:`, a clause that needs a block as a block, each block clause set apart with a blank line." That sentence now decides opus-1's validate_path!/1 (line 107 `defp validate_path!("/" <> _rest), do: :ok` beside two raise blocks set apart by blank lines, lines 109-111 and 113-115) as clean; in 2026-10-22-c the same shape in opus-1 and sonnet-1 was violated under the removed most-clauses sentence. Every mixed function in all five files (segment matchers in every run, validate_path!/1 in opus-1) sets each block clause apart with a blank line, so the mix sentence is broken 0 of 5. The one violation (haiku-1) is decided by the unchanged sentences "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line" and "The same holds for `if`: `if ..., do: ..., else: ...` fits when each branch is one short expression on the `if`'s line".

do: rule, per sentence: one-expression do: bodies: 0 of 5 broken (every do: body is one call, literal, match or boolean expression; no do: on a multi-step body). Multi-step, case or comment bodies on do:: 0 of 5. Mix sentence: 0 of 5. Head's-line sentence and if sentence: 1 of 5, haiku-1 lines 77-78 `if not module_name?(handler),` / `do: invalid!(module, "handler must be a module name", handler)`; joined at its depth it is 96 characters and Code.format_string! keeps it on one line, so mix format did not force the wrap; the transcript shows haiku-1 wrote the wrap itself in its Write call. grep for lines starting with do: or else: finds only that line in the five files. Guard-wrap sentence: not exercised (no head is broken after a guard). Every one-expression do ... end block in the five files was rewritten as a do: line at its real nesting depth and run through Code.format_string!: all wrap (opus-1 generated match/1 114, validate_path!/1 raise clauses 139 and 113, the validate_handler! if 175, module_name?/1 111, match_segments blocks 160 and 133; haiku-1 generated match/1 105, invalid!/3 128, bind blocks 123 and 135; haiku-2 ifs 146 and 192, bind blocks 130 and 99; sonnet-1 generated match/1 131, __define__/3 raise clauses 145 and 131, match_segments blocks 140 and 125; sonnet-2 generated match/1 101, ifs 105 and 122, match_segments blocks 144 and 141), so no block is a judgement call this sweep. haiku-2 first wrote `defp bind([literal | pattern], [literal | segments], params), do: bind(pattern, segments, params)`, saw mix format move it, and rewrote it as a block (lines 119-121), the step the new Formatting bullet asks for.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run: the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex (so xref line numbers match the run file) plus real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex. opus-1 and sonnet-1 (Macro.expand_literals with function {:match, 1}) and sonnet-2 (with {:routes, 0}) report alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime). haiku-1 and haiku-2 never expand the handler and pass the alias into a call that runs in the router's module body: haiku-1 lib/tiny_router.ex:129: alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile); haiku-2 lib/tiny_router.ex:129: alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile). All five compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors.

All ten fail with ArgumentError while the router compiles, raised from the @doc false function get's quote calls (haiku-2 through validate_route!/3).

No run is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens this sweep.
